caption:
All you see is the other woman handling motherhood so “effortlessly” while you cry for the third time today. It’s so easy to begin to believe that she must be more motherly and stronger than you could ever be. And yet, her baby sleeps. Her partner has flexible hours. Her family jumps in the moment she needs help. She hasn’t been through the trauma you have and her nervous system has more tolerance. She’s carrying a completely different load than you are - it’s not even comparable. 

With my first baby, I felt like I couldn’t cope and that meant I was a failure. Nevermind the fact that it was 2020, my baby never slept, and PPD/PPA was plaguing my every day. 

Then fast forward to my third baby - the hardest of all three - and yet, I’m experiencing so much joy this time around. 

Because I know me struggling, especially compared to others who seem to thrive, is not evidence of my worth (or lack of). It’s simply a natural reaction to what I’m carrying. And that’s okay ❤️

okay but hear me out…

No, but seriously, wait for it (and put down your pitch fork omg)

Any time I’ve seen my friends postpartum, I’ve never once felt like they “were behind” or “looked awful” or “gave up on themselves”. To be honest, I wasn’t even focused on their body or appearance because that’s not why I’m their friend (and their little baby was too cute to notice anything else). 

So why in the world must we be soooo hard on ourselves? This is the most I’ve gained in any pregnancy and the most I’ve weighed in my life. It’s jarring. My new clothing size number is jarring. The way so many of my clothes do not fit IS jarring.

But I know I’ll never shame myself into getting fit (especially as someone who holds onto weight while breastfeeding). So I might as well be kind to myself, no? 

I don’t know, some days I’m crushing this mentality and other days I’m weeping in my closet but it is some food for thought!

caption:
I remember googling, “when does it get easier?”

I remember loving my baby deeply
and still feeling completely overwhelmed.

The 2am tears.
The second-guessing.
The wondering if I was cut out for this.

I think we’re sometimes scared to say this out loud:

You CAN love your baby
and still not love how hard motherhood feels.

If that’s you right now, I was you 🫶🏼❤️

And it’s so easy to feel guilty in this season. When people say “just wait, you’ll miss this” or “soak it up,” and you’re barely keeping your head above water, you start to wonder what’s wrong with you. Why this doesn’t feel magical?!

But struggling doesn’t make you ungrateful.
And not enjoying every moment doesn’t mean you love your baby any less.

This season doesn’t magically become easy.
But it stretches. It grows. So do you. 🤍

And one day you’ll look around at the life you built and think:

“Wow. We made it.”

It’s so worth it.

caption:
Yesterday I caught myself feeling really discouraged while scrolling.

My feed was full of routines, systems, productivity tips… ways to get your life together, keep your house spotless, lose the baby weight, anything to optimize motherhood.

And honestly?
A lot of it is good advice.

But in that moment my baby was fussy as heck and any time I tried to be “productive” it left both of us upset. 

Because she didn’t need a better routine or a cleaner house or a more productive version of me.

She just needed to be held.

So I’m trying to remind myself that motherhood has seasons.

And currently I’m in one that is meant to slow me down. And thank God for that because I have my whole life to do allll the things but I only have this short window to truly soak up this version of my tiny humans that will soon be a faded memory. 

So maybe this is exactly where I’m supposed to be. ❤️

Ingredients: 
1 cup butter, softened
3⁄4 cup brown sugar
1⁄2 cup white sugar
2 eggs
2 tsp vanilla extract
21⁄4 cups all-purpose flour
1⁄2 cup cocoa powder
1 tsp baking soda
1⁄4 tsp salt
Reese’s Mini Cups or Chocolate truffles
Mini pretzels (for legs)
Candy eyes (I love the Wilton’s brand) 
Optional: black icing for decorating! 

Instructions: 

🎃1) Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).

👻2) In a large bowl, cream together butter and both sugars until light and fluffy.

🍁3) Beat in eggs one at a time, then add vanilla.

🎃4) In another bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt. Gradually mix dry ingredients into the wet mixture.

👻5) Roll dough into small balls and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 8–10 minutes.

🍁6) Once baked, immediately press a chocolate truffle or Reese’s cup into the center of each cookie (this will be the spider’s body).

🎃7) While still warm, gently press broken pretzel pieces into the sides as spider legs.

👻8) Let cool completely, then attach candy eyes using a bit of melted chocolate or icing

caption:
The truth is, I saw my husband loving me by taking care of the kids, our home, working hard, and so much more, but a part of me still felt unseen. Obviously, I was grateful but my love language is words of affirmation and well…my husband’s is not. It’s not something that come naturally to him. And without having that part of me filled, despite all the areas I was appreciative, something felt missing…

And from this struggle, this letter was written. A letter filled with words that he meant and felt, but didn’t always know how to express. Which were words I so desperately needed to hear spoken out loud.

And now I share it because it’s not just for me…it’s for: 
♥️ the one who is like me with a loving partner who isn’t the most “wordy” 
♥️ to the one who DESERVES these words from their partner but knows they’ll never get them 
♥️ to the one who hears things about themself that tear down - this video…this letter…is who you are, this is what you radiate…this is what you deserve. 
♥️ and to the one who doesn’t have support but is worthy every word said 

I pray these words can make you feel seen for all that you do and sacrifice. You are making magic, every single day for your family. Even in the mundane or the hard moments. Don’t give up, don’t think lowly of yourself or what you have to offer. 

You’re making a far greater difference than you realize 🫶🏼

caption:
I filmed this in December but was too embarrassed to even edit it because of my lil menty-b caught on camera. But the more I’ve sat on it, the more I’ve wondered how many of us push ourselves to a breaking point regularly? 

We know balance is key but we aren’t actually ready to accept that balance sometimes requires sacrificing the standard we hold ourself to. Because we can’t value both rest and perfectionism. We have to let go of something - whether that’s your ideal or yourself. It’s a choice. 

So there I was, pushing myself way too hard at work, striving to make the Christmas season magical, trying to keep a tidy home, trying to be a decent parent and wife and friend and human being…and I snapped. I was so tired. So low. So done.

And the recovery time that was required after hitting this breaking point was far more extensive than I expected. There was a cost to not evaluating my expectations and adjusting them to match the fact that I AM A HUMAN BEINNNNGGG. Jeez. 

So yes. Rest isn’t a reward for all your doing. It’s actually a necessary need to have before, during, and after so that you can have longevity AND avoid alllll the menty-b goodness.

caption:
I spent my baby’s first year of life constantly terrified I was ruining him. The internet and people around me were loud about the bad habits I was creating with sleep, soothers, feeding, blah blah blah blah. Instead of enjoying all the cuddles, or nursing them to sleep, or letting them have the comfort of their soother, I was an anxious mess. 

Four years later? 

My kid sleeps through the night and can go to sleep on his own (but we choose to lie with him). He dropped the soother at 3 like a champ and didn’t look back. Nursing to sleep did nothing except help me get him to sleep easily as a baby. And even waiting to potty train until I felt he was ready instead of when the internet told me I should, resulted in a really easy experience. 

It’s not to say there weren’t challenges that came with changing those “bad habits” but I can confidently say, it wasn’t half as bad as the internet will make you feel. 

There is a solution to everything. It’s okay to choose to lean into what is working and run with it for now. ♥️ you will figure it out.
